title: 💾 Son Considered Buying SK Hynix for a Trillion Dollars... Then Backed Away!
body: 💾 Son Considered Buying SK Hynix for a Trillion Dollars... Then Backed Away!

A report published on November 20 revealed that Masayoshi Son, chairman of the SoftBank Group, recently contacted major Wall Street financial institutions to explore financing a possible purchase of SK Hynix, the world's second-largest memory chip maker, in a deal that could have been worth about a trillion dollars, or roughly 1,400 trillion Korean won.

But the idea stopped at an early stage: a SoftBank spokesperson said the company considers many opportunities, and that this deal is 'no longer under active consideration'. SK Hynix said it knows nothing about the matter, adding that any foreign acquisition of the company requires prior approval from the Korean government under the law. It was not even confirmed whether the banks had discussed providing the financing at all.

The numbers alone seem enough to explain the retreat: SK Hynix's market value is about $578 billion, after falling sharply from its peak about a month earlier, meaning the proposed trillion equals the peak value plus a control premium of about 40%. The interest reflects a heated race for AI memory, the one piece still missing from SoftBank's AI supply chain, as the company holds stakes in Arm, Intel, and OpenAI, while SK Hynix is one of only three companies that make high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators.
Simply put: a man wanted to buy a company much bigger than his own, then discovered the numbers do not work; so was the idea real ambition, or just testing the waters of the booming memory market?
